notes_context:
Memory items from past tasks:
- [rb-0001] Round money with the project's round_money helper: Monetary results must be rounded via ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent), not Python round() or bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding.
  Before returning any computed money value, wrap it in round_money(...). Check the repo's money module for existing helpers (round_money, to_money, ZERO) and reuse them rather than inventing rounding logic.
- [rb-0008] Compute strictly-after occurrences with floor division plus one: For periodic events anchored at a start time, the first occurrence strictly after a timestamp is start + ((after - start) // period + 1) * period.
  Use integer floor division on timedeltas to find the index of the period containing `after`, then add one to get the next boundary. Handle the before-start case separately by returning start + period, since the start itself is not a renewal.
- [rb-0004] Mirror existing error codes and validation patterns: Reuse the codebase's established BillingError codes and validation idioms rather than inventing new ones.
  Before writing validation, grep the repo for existing BillingError codes (e.g. invalid_state, non_positive_amount) and copy the same code strings and message formats. Consistency with sibling functions like issue_invoice/authorize makes hidden tests that assert on error codes pass.
- [rb-0006] Normalize money inputs via to_money before comparing: Convert unit_price with the project's to_money helper before sign checks so strings/Decimals are handled uniformly.
  Call to_money(unit_price) first, then compare against ZERO for negativity; this reuses existing conversion/rounding and raises the project's invalid_amount error for unparseable input instead of a raw exception.
- [rb-0010] Check idempotency key before any validation: When implementing money-moving operations, look up the idempotency key in the audit log first and return the original result before validating state or amount.
  Team convention requires an optional keyword-only idempotency_key=None on every operation that moves money or changes a balance. Scan audit.events() for a matching key first; if found, return the original record without reapplying. Include idempotency_key in the audit entry you write.
- [rb-0012] Mirror sibling module conventions when implementing stubs: Before implementing a NotImplementedError stub, read sibling functions (e.g. payments.authorize) and reuse their money helpers, error codes, and audit patterns.
  Reuse round_money/to_money/ZERO from money.py, BillingError codes like invalid_state and non_positive_amount, ensure_utc for timestamps, and audit.record with a consistent event name. This keeps new functions consistent with the codebase and hidden tests.

item.title: Reuse existing money helpers for rounding and coercion
item.description: When adding a monetary function, reuse the repo's to_money/round_money/ZERO helpers instead of ad-hoc float math.
item.content: Search for a money module before implementing arithmetic. Coercing inputs with to_money and rounding with round_money guarantees consistent half-up cent rounding and Decimal handling across the codebase.

item.title: Match existing BillingError code conventions
item.description: Grep sibling modules for BillingError usage to pick error codes consistent with the project's style.
item.content: Before raising errors, grep for `BillingError(` to see established codes like `non_positive_amount` or `invalid_state`. Choose a similarly named code (e.g. `invalid_rate`) and pass the offending value as the message.

item.title: Verify boundary and rounding edge cases before submitting
item.description: Run quick manual checks for inclusive bounds, half-up rounding, and error paths after implementing.
item.content: After writing the function, exercise boundary values (0 and 100), a half-cent rounding case, and invalid inputs to confirm behavior. This catches off-by-one range checks and rounding-mode mistakes that hidden tests often probe.
